title: Fermat's Last Theorem
statement: For every integer n greater than 2, there are no positive integers a, b, c with a^n + b^n = c^n.

formal.statement: (forall ((n Int) (a Int) (b Int) (c Int)) (=> (and (> n 2) (> a 0) (> b 0) (> c 0)) (not (= (+ (pow a n) (pow b n)) (pow c n)))))

provenance.source: written to exercise external_status; the `facts-number` extraction lane reached this concept and correctly refused to record it, because before external_status every available status would have been false

prior_art.what: Modular elliptic curves and Fermat's Last Theorem
prior_art.notes: With Richard Taylor, 'Ring-theoretic properties of certain Hecke algebras', Annals of Mathematics 141 (3): 553-572, which repairs the gap in the original 1993 announcement.

notes:
The point of this entry is the status pair, not the theorem. `epistemic_status: open` says axeyum has not established it; `external_status: proved` says mathematics has. Before the second field, this fact was unwritable: `proved` would have claimed our kernel checked Wiles, `open` would have implied the question is unsettled, and `conjectured` would have been false since 1995.

It also marks a real boundary rather than a bookkeeping one. `formal.fragment` is `none`: nothing in this system decides it, and `pow` with a variable exponent is outside every fragment we implement. The statement is recorded in SMT-LIB shape anyway so the gap is legible and greppable -- an honest `none` is more useful than an omission, because it can be counted.

The self-extension loop must filter on `epistemic_status == open AND external_status != proved`, or it will spend its queue re-deriving the settled literature.
